17. The learned Counsel further submits that the plaintiff has got no title and possession over the suit land and the plaintiff miserably failed to prove his title and also possession. Although the plaintiff claims that she is in possession of the suit land and produced two rent receipts, one of 1986 and another of 1990, that is not the proof of his possession. Next he submits although the plaintiff claims that he has mutated his name by Mutation Case No. 1060/74 but the plaintiff could not produce any certified copy of mutated khatian or any rough paper of mutated khatian.  23. The plaintiff examined as many as 6 witnesses in this case to prove the case. Shahamat Ali Karikar was examined as PW 3 who was said to be an attesting witness. The learned trial Court observed that since the original deed was not produced his signature could not be compared with original deed. PW 2 stated in his evidence that the vendor of the plaintiff Hari Sadhan never went to India and still he is living in Bangladesh and Hari Sadhan has been living in the same village of the plaintiff and in that case the plaintiff ought to have examined Hari Sadhan to prove the genuineness of the registered kabala dated 2-9-70. The recommendation made by the ADC (Revenue) to release the property from the list of the vested property has got no basis because although the plaintiff claimed that she was possessing the suit land by mutating her name by Mutation Case No. 1060/74 but the plaintiff could not produce any certified copy of the mutation khatian or any rough mutation khatian. The plaintiff produced 2 rent receipts, one of 1986 and another of 1990, but the claim of the plaintiff is that he purchased the land in the year 1970 but no rent receipt except in 1986 and 1990 could be produced by the plaintiff. The trial Court rightly observed that the plaintiff had no continuous possession over the suit land. The plaintiff's case has got two phases: first phase of the plaintiff's case is that the plaintiff purchased the suit land from Hari Sadhan by a registered kabala dated 2-9-70 and the second phase is to treat the property as vested property. Thereafter, while the plaintiff was enjoying the property, abruptly in the year 1980 the vested property authority treated this property as vested property and enlisted the property in the vested property list and thereafter, leased out the suit property to one Nur Mohammad vide VP Case No. 600 (kali)/ 8081. Now the question is, whether the plaintiff has been able to prove his title over the suit property by the certified copy of the kabala dated 2-9-70. In this connection, I like to rely on the case of Sova Rani Guha alias Sova Rani Gupta vs Abdul Awal Miah and others reported in 1994 BLD (AD) 257 wherein it has been held that section 63—Secondary evidence —"The production of the certified copy of a sale deed does not by itself warrant the presumption of due execution of the original document A party producing the Secondary evidence of a document is not relieved of the duty of proving the execution of the original. Even in a case where a document has been exhibited without objection the court is to be satisfied as to the execution of the document." In the instant case, to prove the genuineness of the document onus is upon the plaintiff to produce Hari Sadhan who executed the deed in absence of the original one but the plaintiff could not produce Hari Sadhan before the court as witness. The lower appellate Court while reversing the judgment of the trial Court ought to have assigned in his judgment justifying the reason in reversing the judgment of the trial Court, particularly in respect of the title deed. But the lower appellate Court in reversing the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court did not assign any cogent reason and also did not consider the evidence on record, particularly the evidence of PW 2 affecting the merit of the case. In this connection, I like to rely on the decision in the case of Most Mohsina Khatun vs Ms Habib Knitting Mills reported in 1997 BLD (AD) 47 wherein it is stated that while reversing the judgment of the trial Court the appellate Court is required to reverse the material findings of the trial Court with reference to evidence on record. The judgment of the trial Court transpires that in arriving at its finding the said Court carefully considered the material facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record, both oral and documentary, and the certified copy of the original title deed of the plaintiff. The learned trial Court did not commit any error of law and illegality in arriving at its finding because the plaintiff could not be able to prove his case. The lower appellant Court without considering the evidence on record and without proper assessment of the evidence and also without considering the title deed was not proved and came to an erroneous finding which is liable to be interfered by this Court.
